Several other lens observations were reviewed and dropped as non-blocking: gatewayKey exposure in both output modes is the explicit, spec-approved deliverable (dismissed — not a new secret-handling regression); undefined-field handling for gatewayKey/startedAt and the reason/lastRecordedIssue data-source conflation all mirror pre-existing, unchanged code patterns in the same file rather than being introduced by this diff (deferred, 4 items); the loosely-typed Record<string, unknown> payload and the tautological uptimeSec test assertion are minor and non-blocking (dismissed/deferred, 2 items). No standards or security guide violations found.

findings.title: Byte-identical test doesn't verify byte-identical output
findings.problem: The test 'leaves the default (non-JSON) output byte-identical aside from the new API Key line' only asserts `expect(lines).toContain(...)` for 4 specific lines, with no check on line count, order, or completeness.
findings.impact: The test would still pass if extra lines were added, existing lines were reordered, or other lines were altered, so it does not actually back up its own name or enforce the spec's core non-regression requirement ('preserve the existing human-readable output byte-for-byte when --json is not passed').
findings.recommendation: Replace the toContain checks with a full-array assertion (e.g. `expect(lines).toEqual([...])` listing every expected line in order, or join and compare against the fixed expected human-readable string) so the test genuinely fails if any other line changes.
